title: Geoff Britton is fired from Wings | 1975
content:
Wings’ second drummer Geoff Britton was fired from the band on 22 January 1975.

He had been recruited via a series of auditions in London, and joined the band on 16 May 1974. However, the teetotal Britton’s playing and personality were at odds with the band’s hard-living attitude, and Paul McCartney eventually decided he was the wrong fit for Wings.

Paul and Linda McCartney told Britton of the decision at their hotel, Le Richelieu, in New Orleans.

Paul and Linda turned up and gave me the sack, as yesterday’s track hadn’t gone right. I wasn’t knocking them out. It was just based on that. Great guy, etc. At first, Paul wants me to move out the same day then realized that’s mean and I can stay and sort things out. Alan [Crowder] and Marshall [Sehorn] hung around with me that afternoon.
Geoff Britton’s diary, 23 January 1975
The McCartney Legacy: Volume 2: 1974-80

Britton’s replacement, Joe English, arrived in New Orleans later this evening, and took part in his first Wings recording session on 23 January 1975.

Britton was offered £1,000 in addition to his session fees and expenses. He later accepted a much higher settlement. He remained in New Orleans until early February before flying back to London.

MPL issued a press release, dictated by Paul McCartney to Tony Brainsby:

The parting is amicable. Geoff wants to work on his own project. It is a film about karate, and he hopes to start shooting it at the end of March. He is writing the musical score which will be percussion based. The film will be shot abroad, and Geoff’s involvement will be extensive. It was an opportunity he didn’t want to turn down, especially as it could open up a completely new career for him. Paul and Linda fully appreciated this, and the parting was completely amicable.
